Items.Description:
TOPCOACH IN BRIEF

Use your budget to select an 18-man squad filled with players who you expect to score points for you regularly throughout the season. You can choose a maximum of four players from each club. 

Once the season starts, the numbers of points your players score will be dependent on their real-life performances in each particular Gameweek. They will score points if they score a goal, provide an assist, keep a clean sheet etc., but points can also be deducted for conceding goals, picking up yellow/red cards etc.

Every Gameweek you must:

  • Select your starting XI. All the points these players score will be added to your weekly total.
  • Select four substitutes (one for each position). Only half the points these players score will be added to your weekly total.
  • Your three non-selected players won’t score any points for you in that particular Gameweek.
  • Choose from the following formations: 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 3-4-3 or 3-5-2. Your formation will automatically change if you replace a player in a different position whilst making your selection.
  • Select a captain. This player's score will be doubled in a regular Gameweek or trebled if it's one of our four Super Gameweeks. Be warned though, the number of minus points they score will also be doubled (or trebled in Super Gameweeks).
  • Predict the correct score of our Match of the Week, which could earn you additional points.

 

FIRST HALF OF THE SEASON

The season starts with a period in which you can make unlimited transfers.

Player values after Gameweek 2
The Tuesday after Gameweek 2, player values will be finalised. If the valuation of a player in your squad decreases, that difference in value will be added back to your budget. In exceptional cases, the value of a player could also increase. If that occurs, they will automatically be removed from your squad and their initial value will be added back to your budget. There is one exception: If a player is transferred to another team within the league, their value could change, even if it takes place after Gameweek 2. The same rules as above will apply if their value increases/decreases.

Two lowest Gameweek scores
Your two lowest Gameweek scores during this period will be deleted and not count towards your end-of-season total. If you join the game after the season has started, you won't score any points for the Gameweeks you've missed and those scores will be included when calculating your two lowest-scoring Gameweeks.

Transfer market closing
From the first Gameweek after the international break in September, your team is official and you can no longer transfer players till the winter break.

 

SECOND HALF OF THE SEASON

After the last Gameweek of the year, the winter break starts.

Player values
Players can increase or decrease in value during the second transfer window, depending on their performances, and their club's performances, during the first half of the season. This increase or decrease does not have an impact on your budget. With the same budget, everyone gets the chance to create a new top team for the second half of the season.

Every Gameweek counts
During the winter break, your scores in every Gameweek will count towards your total score, and your two lowest Gameweek scores will not be deleted like they are in the first transfer window.

Transfer market closing
From the first Gameweek after 31 January, your team is official and you can no longer transfer players.

Items.Title: Points

Items.Description:
SQUAD SELECTION

Use your budget to select an 18-man squad filled with players who you expect to score points for you regularly throughout the season. You can choose a maximum of four players from each club. 

 

GAMEWEEK SELECTIONS

Every Gameweek you must:

  • Select your starting XI. All the points these players score will be added to your weekly total.
  • Select four substitutes (one for each position). Only half the points these players score will be added to your weekly total.
  • Your three non-selected players won’t score any points for you in that particular Gameweek.
  • Your starting XI must adhere to one of the following formations: 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 3-4-3 or 3-5-2. Your formation will automatically change if you replace a player in a different position whilst making your selection.
  • Select a captain. This player's score will be doubled in a regular Gameweek or trebled if it's one of the four Super Gameweeks. Be warned though, the number of points deductions will also be doubled (or trebled in Super Gameweeks).
  • Predict your Match of the Week, which could earn you additional points.

 

POINTS PER GAMEWEEK

There are various ways your players can score (or lose) points for you, and you can also gain additional points by correctly predicting the outcome to our 'Match of the Week' in each particular Gameweek. 

Here's a run through of how you can score points:

1. GOALS SCORED

Players are awarded points for every goal they score, and if they manage to score a hat-trick they'll receive an additional bonus on top.

Players will be deducted points if they score an own goal (an no, any own goals will not count towards hat-tricks!).

An own goal is only assigned to a player if their opponent's last touch of the ball was not an attempt on goal, or that attempt on goal would have been highly unlikely to result in a goal if the own goal scorer hadn't made contact with the ball. 

The term super-sub refers to a real-life player who starts a match as a substitute but comes on for less than 45 minutes in regular time and plays a decisive part in it such as scoring a goal, saving a penalty, providing an assist etc. If that happens, your super-sub's score in that particular Gameweek will be doubled. Conversely, if they come on as a substitute and score an own goal, miss a penalty etc., those points deductions will also be doubled. 

 

2. ASSISTS

Assist points are only awarded to a player who makes the final pass or contribution which results in his own club scoring a goal.

The number of points awarded for an assist will be doubled if that player is a super-sub (see the 'Goals' section above for more details about what a super-sub is).

Please refer to our Assist Guide for full details regarding assists.

 

3. PENALTIES

All players who convert a penalty kick receive the same number of points, regardless of their position. A player who misses a penalty kick receives negative points. A penalty kick that is scored on the second attempt counts as a missed penalty kick and as a regular goal.


A goalkeeper who saves a penalty kick receives points for this, even if the penalty kick is missed without the goalkeeper's involvement.

A pinch hitter, someone who started as a substitute for his club but entered the field and played less than 45 minutes within regular playing time, receives double points per penalty kick converted, missed or saved.

 

4. CARDS

Players will be deducted points if they are shown yellow or red cards. Points deducted for a straight red card are double those of a yellow card, and if a player is shown a red card after two yellow cards, they will only be deducted points for the two yellow cards. 

If it's unclear initially, which player has been shown a card, Scorito will wait for official confirmation.

 

5. PLAYING TIME

Players score points for being on the pitch for at least 45 minutes of a match (excluding stoppage time), irrespective of whether they featured as a substitute or not.  

 

6. TEAM PERFORMANCE

Players score points for a win or a draw if they were on the pitch for at least 45 minutes of that match (excluding stoppage time), irrespective of whether they featured as a substitute or not. No points are awarded or deducted if their team loses that match.

 

7. CLEAN SHEETS

Goalkeepers, defenders and midfielders will score points if their team keeps a clean sheet (i.e. doesn't concede a goal) in a particular match. To score those points however, a player needs to have been on the pitch for at least 45 minutes of that match (excluding stoppage time), irrespective of whether they featured as a substitute or not.

 

8. CONCEDING GOALS

Goalkeepers, defenders and midfielders will have points deducted for every two goals they concede. To be deducted those points however, a player needs to have been on the pitch for at least 45 minutes of that match (excluding stoppage time), irrespective of whether they featured as a substitute or not. 

 

9. MATCH OF THE WEEK

Each Gameweek, you could score extra points by correctly predicting the outcome of our Match of the Week.

1) Players score 64 points if they correctly predict the winning team or draw.
2) Players score 128 points for correctly predicting the exact result.

 

FIRST HALF OF THE SEASON

The season starts with a period in which players can make unlimited transfers.

Player values after Gameweek 2
The Tuesday after Gameweek 2, player values will be finalised. If the valuation of a player in a player's squad decreases, that difference in value will be added back to his/her budget. In exceptional cases, the value of a player could also increase. If that occurs, they will automatically be removed from the squad and their initial value will be added back to the budget. There is one exception: If a player is transferred to another team within the league, their value could change, even if it takes place after Gameweek 2. The same rules as above will apply if their value increases/decreases.

Two lowest Gameweek scores
The two lowest Gameweek scores during this period will be deleted and not count towards the end-of-season total. If a player joins the game after the season has started, he/she won't score any points for the Gameweeks he/she missed and those scores will be included when calculating the two lowest-scoring Gameweeks.

Transfer market closing
From the first Gameweek after the international break in September, the player's team is official and no players can be transferred until the winter break.

 

SECOND HALF OF THE SEASON

During the winter break, the transfer market is open again and participants can make unlimited transfers.

Player values
Players can increase or decrease in value during the second transfer window, depending on their performances, and their club's performances, during the first half of the season. This increase or decrease does not have an impact on a player's budget. With the same budget, everyone gets the chance to create a new top team for the second half of the season.

Every Gameweek counts
During the winter break, the scores in every Gameweek will count towards the total score, and the two lowest Gameweek scores will not be deleted like they are in the first transfer window.

Transfer market closing
From the first Gameweek after 31 January, the player's team is official and no players can be transferred anymore.

 

POSTPONED / ABANDONED MATCHES

If a match is postponed or abandoned, the scores from the rescheduled match will be counted in its original Gameweek, irrespective of when it is eventually played. You also won't be able to change your original team selection for the rescheduled match. If the first match of a Gameweek is postponed, the original deadline of the Gameweek remains.

Only scores from the rescheduled match will count towards your score. Any points from the original game which was abandoned will be deleted. 

If the match is never concluded, Scorito will defer to the Eredivisie's decision regarding the outcome of the match.

A Gameweek only concludes once all the matches in that particular Gameweek have been completed.

 

PROCESSING RESULTS

Match data
Scorito receives match data from a company called Gracenote who are an independent, marketing-leading supplier of sports data.

Goalscorers/cautions
Scorito defers to the Eredivisie's official data in determining which players have scored goals and/or received yellow/red cards.

If the Eredivisie change any of their decisions, so too will Scorito, and the scores could also change as a result. Scorito will only make those changes however, if they occur before the start of the subsequent Gameweek, or within 24 hours of the final match of the season concluding. If the Eredivisie make any changes after those times, Scorito will not make those changes.

Assists
Scorito receives data on goal assists from a company called Gracenote (see above), but ultimately follows its own 'Assist Guide'. If, once a particular Gameweek has concluded and there are still doubts being raised about an assist, Scorito will make a request for Gracenote to reassess the situation and explain how they came to their decision. In the meantime, Scorito will also reassess the situation themselves, and should Scorito assess the situation differently to Gracenote, Scorito's decision will ultimately be final. 

 

EQUAL SCORES

If two players are level on points in their league(s), the player who signed up for the game first will be listed highest in the table.

 

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

The same terms and conditions are applied for every game on Scorito. These terms and conditions can be found on the Scorito app and website. If any matters arise where the terms and conditions are deemed inconclusive, the management at Scorito.com Nederland BV will decide on the outcome and any such decision is not subject to appeal.
Items.Title: Rules

Items.Description:
1. Assists

General definition
1.1 Assist points are only awarded to a player who makes the final pass or contribution which results in his own club scoring a goal.

Considerations
1.2 An assist can only be credited to a goalscorer's team-mate, not an opposing player.
1.3 Winning a penalty/free kick that results in a goal does not count as an assist.
1.4 No assist points are awarded for passes or contributions which result in own goals.
1.5 If there is considerable doubt whether or not an assist should be awarded, Scorito will award that assist.
1.6 It doesn't matter if the pass or contribution which resulted in a goal is intentional or not.  
1.7 If a player who deflected a team-mate's shot is credited with the goal, the original player's shot will counted as an assist.

 

2. Interceptions

General definition
2.1 The goalscorer intercepted the ball from an opponent before scoring.

Exceptions to the rule
2.1.1 If the final touch before the goalscorer received the ball was a save or block(ed shot), the goal is classified as a rebound, and the player that pre-empted that save or block will not be awarded an assist.
2.1.2 If the last touch before the goalscorer received the ball was a slight deflection off an opponent, an assist will still be awarded to the player who made the original pass (see below).

 

3. Common situations

Pass deflected by an opponent
3.1 Although the last player to touch the ball before the goalscorer received the ball was an opponent, a deflected pass or cross will still be awarded as an assist if:
3.1.1 the team-mate was originally directing their pass to the goalscorer, and/or...
3.1.2 the opponent only deflected the ball very lightly and it didn't significantly influence the flight of the ball. 

Pass deflected by a team-mate
3.2 Generally, the last player to touch the ball before the goalscorer received it will be awarded with the assist. However, an exception to this rule would be if Player A's pass was intended to reach the goalscorer but Player B (a team-mate) deflected the ball very slightly on its way to the goalscorer. In this situation, we would award the assist to Player A. If Player B's deflection significantly changed the speed and/or direction of Player A's pass, Player B would be awarded with the assist. 

Ball intercepted by an opponent
3.3 If an opposing player touches the ball after the goalscorer has received it from a team-mate, but before he's shot, the opponent’s touch could prove decisive.
3.3.1 If that touch clearly causes the goalscorer to lose control of the ball (even momentarily) before recovering it and scoring the goal, the goal is classified as an interception and the original pass will not count as an assist.
3.3.2 If the opponent’s touch doesn't make the goalscorer lose control of the ball before he scores, then his team-mate who passed the ball to him will be awared the assist. 

 

4. Further examples

Rebounds
4.1 Goals resulting from the following situations are classed as rebounds, and not assists: 
4.1.1 If a player's original pass, shot or cross is blocked or saved by an opponent, or hits the woodwork, before reaching the goalscorer.
4.1.2 If a player's original pass, shot or cross is deflected by an opponent before being blocked, saved or hitting the woodwork, and then reaching the goalscorer.

4.2 If a goal is scored after an earlier shot was saved, blocked or hit the woodwork and resulted in a loose ball, it is classed as a rebound and not an assist. This is also the case if the ball is rebounded to the goalscorer outside the penalty box, or if the goalscorer dribbles the ball before scoring.

Free kicks
4.3 A goal has no assist if it is scored directly from a free kick.
4.3.1 If a player passes an indirect free kick to the goalscorer and no-one else touches the ball before the goalscorer shoots, then the free kick taker will be awarded an assist. 

Corners
4.4 A goal has no assist if it is scored directly from a corner kick.
4.4.1 If a player takes a corner which immediately results in a goal, then that corner taker will be awarded with an assist.

Penalties
4.5 A goal has no assist if it is scored directly from a penalty kick.
4.5.1 If a player misses a penalty but his team-mate scores directly from the rebound, the goal will be classified as a rebound and not an assist.

Items.Description:
Joining private leagues for our games is very easy. To do so, simply follow these steps:

 

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage
  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen

  • Click on the 'Join a league' button and search for the name of the league you want to join, or the player's name who has organised that league

  • You can join public leagues immediately by clicking the green cross next to that league's name

  • You can only join private leagues if you get permission from the organiser to do so. You can request permission by clicking on the green cross next to that league's name

 

If you can't find a private league by searching for its name or organiser, it's because the organiser has probably chosen to hide it. If that occurs, you'll have to contact the organiser directly to try and get an invitation.
Items.Title: How do I join private leagues?

Items.Description: If you can't find a private league by searching for its name or organiser, it's because the organiser has probably chosen to hide it. If that occurs, you'll have to contact the organiser directly to try and get an invitation.
Items.Title: What if I can't find a private league?

Items.Description:
Viewing your league position(s) is very easy. To do so, simply follow these steps:

 

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage

  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen

  • Click on the league you want to view your position in by clicking on it in the 'My leagues' section
Items.Title: How do I view my league position(s)?

Items.Description: No, every player is only able to make one set of predictions per account for each stage of the tournament.
Items.Title: Can I make different picks for different leagues?

Items.Description:
First check if the organiser has accepted your request to join their league! They should have received that request in their ‘Management’ section of the league.

 

If they have already accepted you, wait until the table has been updated (after the next match) and you should have appeared. If not, please contact our Online Help Desk via the following steps:

 

  • Click on the account icon in the top-right corner of the app/mobile website/Game Centre
  • Click on Help & contact
  • Click on Contact form
Items.Title: I've joined but can’t see myself in a league?

Items.Description:
Yes, but you must have joined the game before the event started. If you didn’t join the game before the start of the event, you can’t.

 

If you are able to join the league you’ll keep all your original points (they won’t be reset to zero).
Items.Title: Can I join leagues after the event starts?

Items.Description:
Deleting yourself from a private league is very easy. To do so, simply follow these steps:

 

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage

  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen

  • Click on the league you want to delete yourself from in the 'My leagues' section

  • Click on the 'League info' tab

  • Click on the red 'Leave league' button
Items.Title: How do I delete myself from a private league?

Items.Description:
Organising a private league for one of our games is very easy. To do this, simply follow these steps:

 

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage
  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen
  • Click on 'Create private league'
Items.Title: How do I create a private league?

Items.Description:
Managing your private league is very easy. To do this, simply follow these steps:

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage
  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen
  • Click on the name of your private league in the 'My leagues' section
  • Click on the Management tab

 

Here you can:

 

  • Invite more players
  • Find and copy your league’s unique link
  • View the players in your league
  • See if your players have completed their predictions
  • Accept new players into your league
  • Remove players from your league
  • Send messages everyone in your league
  • Adjust your league info
Items.Title: Where do I manage my private league?

Items.Description:
Inviting players to join your league is very easy. To do this, simply follow these steps:

 

  • Once you've logged in, open the game in either the 'My Games' or 'Game Calendar' sections of the homepage
  • Click on the 'Podium' icon on the grey bar which runs along the foot of the screen
  • Click on the name of your private league in the 'My leagues' section
  • Click on the ‘Management’ tab
  • Click on the ‘Invite’ button

 

Here you can copy your league’s unique invite link, and you can also send invites to friends who’ve joined your leagues in the past.
Items.Title: How do I invite players to join my league?

Items.Description:
First double-check whether you’ve invited them by clicking on the ‘Invite players’ button in your league management page.

If you have already invited them, they might not appear in your league table until it’s been updated (after the next match).

If you’re still experiencing problems, please contact our Online Help Desk via the following steps:

 

  • Click on the account icon in the top-right corner of the app/mobile website/Game Centre
  • Click on Help & contact
  • Click on Contact form
Items.Title: A player's not appearing in my league

Items.Description:
That player will no longer appear in your league table once it’s next been updated (after the next match).

If that doesn’t happen, please contact our Online Help Desk via the following steps:

 

  • Click on the account icon in the top-right corner of the app/mobile website/Game Centre
  • Click on Help & contact
  • Click on Contact form
Items.Title: Why is a player I've deleted still appearing?

Items.Description:
Yes, but we’ll need to do it for you. Please contact our Online Help Desk via the following steps:

 

  • Click on the account icon in the top-right corner of the app/mobile website/Game Centre
  • Click on Help & contact
  • Click on Contact form

 

We don’t let players rejoin leagues manually if they’ve been removed to prevent spamming or trolling.
Items.Title: Can a player I accidentally deleted rejoin?

Items.Description:
Yes you can, the more the merrier! One for your friends, one for your family, one-on-one with your neighbour, etc.

You can only make one set of predictions though, not different ones for different leagues (which we felt would get too time consuming and complicated!).
Items.Title: Can I create multiple private leagues?

Items.Description: Yes it is! You can create as many private leagues as you want, totally free of charge!
Items.Title: Is it free to create a private league?

Items.Description:
Yes, but those players must have joined the game before the event started. If they didn’t join the game before the start of the event, they can’t.

If players do join your league after the deadline they will keep their original points (they won’t be reset to zero).
Items.Title: Can I add players after the event starts?

Items.Description:
Yes, any players you want to join it must have made their initial predictions before the event started. If they didn’t do that, they can’t.

If players do join your league after the deadline they will keep their original points (they won’t be reset to zero).
Items.Title: Can I make leagues after the event starts?
